menu.A: Destroy-and-repair local search: keep one complete solution, repeatedly remove a random subset of its rectangles (and those that depend on them) and regrow greedily; keep the result if it is better.
menu.B: Randomized greedy restarts: build many complete solutions from scratch, choosing each next rectangle at random with a bias toward short perimeters; keep the best solution.
menu.C: Beam search over partial constructions: keep several partial solutions, expand each with a few candidate rectangles, and prune by accumulated weight.
menu.D: Simulated annealing over the sequence of operations with insert and delete moves and a temperature schedule.

menu.A: Simulated annealing over centers and radii: random local moves of one or a few circles from a structured start, accepting by a temperature rule, with radius tightening.
menu.B: Template library: build packings from structured templates (boundary layers and interior rings), fit a few template parameters, then relax and polish locally.
menu.C: Constrained nonlinear optimization of all centers and radii (for example SLSQP) from several starting layouts.
menu.D: Greedy insertion: place circles one at a time, each the largest that fits in the largest remaining gap, then repair locally.
